newsitem.title: USA: First of America Bank to cut 400 jobs; profits up.
newsitem.headline: First of America Bank to cut 400 jobs; profits up.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp. said Tuesday it will cut 400 additional jobs at a cost of $4.0 million to $5.0 million in its ongoing restructuring.
The banking company, based in Kalamazoo, Mich., said it expects to notify the employees by the end of March.

First of America recently notified another 200 employees that their positions will be eliminated in the restructuring. The company had 12,148 full-time equivalent employees as of Dec. 31, 586 fewer than at year-end 1995.
First of America also said its net income rose to $84.0 million, or $1.38 per share, in the fourth quarter, from $66.0 million, or $1.04 per share, in the 1995 period.
The latest results include $14.3 million in after-tax gains from branch sales and one-time charges of $4.2 million associated with severance and various write-downs.
The year-ago results include $9.1 million in gains from branch sales after tax.
First of America is the nation's 32nd-largest banking company, with assets of $22 billion. It serves over 3 million households in Michigan, Illinois, Indiana and Florida.
Its stock edged up 37.5 cents to $59.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
